text:
sara: quick sync — ran the entropy-bucketed coalesce experiment on q2 prod slice, results are a bit surprising 

michael: which slice? the low-latency priority pool or default?

sara: default. traffic mix ~65% short chat, 35% long context generations. baseline was holdtime=2ms, coalesce_delay=1ms, jitter=0.5

tom: can you paste the perf numbers? p50/p95/p99 and kv-hit?

sara: paste below (micro-run, ~1h):
```
baseline: p50=12.0ms p95=46.2ms p99=122.4ms tokens/s=18.2 KV_hit=0.62
entropy-bucketed: p50=11.3ms p95=39.7ms p99=158.7ms tokens/s=19.1 KV_hit=0.58
```

leo: hmm p95 improved but p99 regressed. looks like microburst tails got worse — maybe coalesce grouping increased contention for some kernels

michael: what kernels changed? did scheduler flip from fused-attn to fallback for some sequence lengths?

sara: profiling snapshot shows more small multi-request kernels instead of single large kernel runs. kernel selector favored the generic matmul path in ~18% of windows (vs 7% baseline).

tom: that tracks: entropy bucketing increased variance in per-window seq distribution, kernel selector saw mixed shapes and chose conservative kernels to avoid mispredicted code paths

leo: KV hit drop from .62 -> .58 is small but might amplify p99 if cold-priming happens on tails. Were we priming KV before coalesce?

sara: we disabled prefetch for the test to isolate batching effects. no prefetch.

michael: can we re-run with prefetch enabled + entropy bucketing? hypothesis: prefetch will mask priming latency on tail requests but keep p95 improvements

infra-bot: deploy started: canary entropy-bucketed v2 -> 10% (slice: default)

tom: also try jitter as a function of queue depth (adaptive jitter). when Q>8 set jitter=0.2 else jitter=0.7. Might avoid forming large mixed-shape batches

sara: noted. new config I'm proposing:
```
{"bucket_strategy":"entropy","microwindow_ms":2.5,"coalesce_delay_ms":1.2,"jitter_policy":"adaptive","jitter_params":{"low_q":0.7,"high_q":0.2},"kv_prefetch":true}
```

michael: also add a kernel-selection weight tweak: prefer architecture-optimized kernels when >70% of batch shares seq_len bucket, else prefer fast-generic. small tweak: kernel_prefer_threshold=0.7

leo: for telemetry, record per-window seq_len_entropy, kernel_choice, alloc_count, kv_miss_latency. need to correlate p99 spikes to these tags

sara: I logged a trace slice with those tags during canary. will share link when infra finishes upload.

infra-bot: canary progressed to 10% -> 50% after 14m, no critical errors.

tom: if we still see p99 tail regressions after prefetch + adaptive jitter, we should consider a hedged-coalesce fallback: if batch contains >40% long-context requests, force split into two micro-windows to isolate kernel paths

michael: agree. cheaper than flipping kernel selection heuristics which can ripple. Also add a short cooldown to avoid oscillation.

sara: thanks all — I'll kick off the adaptive-jitter+prefetch run and collect telemetry. quick TODOs: (1) michael add kernel_prefer_threshold flag to selector (2) leo add seq_len_entropy metric to traces (3) tom implement hedged-split prototype

leo: noted and on it.
michael: will PR kernel flag today.

sara: logging the follow-up experiment id: exp/2026-03/entropy-jitter-4

sara: tagging @product for visibility :eyes:
